entries.land_description: housing/permanent structures, plumbing/electricity, camping space, desert land with much vegetation and trees
entries.notes: We are lovers who have lived rurally for the past 10 years. We grow our own food, have milk-goats, chickens, bees, and fruit trees. We live simply and happily, without TV and media, in beautiful desert country with big skies filled with stars. We enjoy visits from lesbians who have an appreciation of rural life and physical work, who are making an effort to eradicate their racist, classist, ageist, anti-Semitic conditioning. We are ethnic women. women working the land.

Raise and sell bees and honey, provide pollination services, make and sell beekeeping equipment. Also breed, raise and train Bashkir Curly horses and standardbred donkeys, plus breed and raise a wide variety of poultry, waterfowl and exotics, including peafowl, rare pheasants and emus. Make and sell mail order t-shirts, caps and rubber stamps relating to bees, donkeys, mules, etc, as well as a line of women's designs. Welcome correspondence from other ranching women; no visitor facilities at present. women living and working on the land.

entries.notes: Inactive group with 23 acres plus some primitive cabins. Many skills to share. Very rural, very private, many camping spaces, and trees. Appreciate work trades for space sharing. Come share and experience the mild central Oregon coast climate, help realize your dreams and mine. Call Carol before 5 am or between 5-8:30 pm. Bon Voyage. I welcome: new members/residents, girl & boy children under control, dogs under 100% control. I have/am: 1 lesbian, 23 acres, housing/permanent structure, electricity, lots of camping space, woods, farmland, women living and working on the land, inactive group with hopes to revive.

entries.land_description: housing/permanent structures, camping space, woods, farmland
entries.welcomed_groups: new members/residents, girl children, boy children upon agreement, nonlesbian women, dogs
entries.notes: (Located in Days Creek, OR ). OWLT is open Women's Land dedicated to provide women access to land, especially those women who otherwise be denied. We are funded by contributions from women around the country. We have a newsletter that is sent quarterly, with an active mailing list of 250 women. At present, we are looking for women to live and work on the land. We are currently raising funds to pay the remaining mortgage, as the former owners (mortgage holders) are threatening us with monthly foreclosure. women living and working on the land.

entries.land_description: housing/permanent structures, plumbing/electricity, camping space, woods, farmland
entries.welcomed_groups: girl children, teens and older lesbians
entries.notes: (13 miles west of Roseburg). We relate independently of one another - we come together for processing big decisions. We all love living in the country in the safety of women's land. We are dedicated to mother nature and are into goddess identification. We preserve the land as wild as much as possible. We love trees and plant often to make up for patriarchal cutting. We bless the land and so appreciate her cradling us. Nature is our best reflection. women living and working on the land.

entries.notes: We are 57 & 60 years old with strong interests in photography, ecology and alternative technology. We enjoy the company and help of women of all ages who can adapt to our simple lifestyle for short or long visits. No guns, drugs, or dope. Smoking limited to outdoor gravel area. We ask $4/day/woman. women living on the land.

entries.land_description: housing/permanent structures, plumbing/electricity, outdoor toilet, camping space, woods, farmland
entries.welcomed_groups: girl children, boy children under age 8, nonlesbian women
entries.notes: WomanShare is a feminist collective of 5-8 lesbians living on forested land in southern Oregon. We have a main house and several women-built cabins and secluded camping spots. The main house has electricity, hot water, and shower. One-to-four day visits when space is available and we ask $3/day for food and $2-10/day for our land support fund. women living and working on the land.
